references.title: The Sumerian Flood Story, segments C-E
references.scope: Oxford ETCSL composite translation; warning, flood, sacrifice and the ending were read with the marked lacunae. No new cuneiform collation or physical-event identification.

references.title: Genesis 9:8-17
references.scope: Read the post-flood covenant in the World English Bible. This is a textual comparison of the promise and its scope, not a geological date.

references.title: Jeremiah 7:1-15
references.scope: Read the temple address in the World English Bible, including conduct and Shiloh. No independent archaeological claim or critical-text collation.

references.title: 1 Corinthians 3:5-17
references.scope: Read the planting, building and temple imagery in its communal context in the World English Bible. No claim that it describes an isolated self-model.

references.title: John 2:19-22
references.scope: Read the narrative identification of the temple with Jesus's body in the World English Bible. Narrative setting and composition date are not equated.

references.title: John 4:19-24
references.scope: Read the competing places of worship and spirit/truth passage in the World English Bible. Its statement about salvation from the Jews is retained.

references.title: Revelation 21:1-4 and 21:22
references.scope: Read the divine dwelling and city without a separate temple in the World English Bible. The constructive interpretation does not establish a transmission route.

references.title: Revelation 22:1-2
references.scope: Read the river, tree and healing of nations in the World English Bible. Practical applications are identified as interpretation, not specified modern policy.

references.title: Luke 22:24-27 and 22:42
references.scope: Read the service contrast and distinction of wills in the World English Bible. No inference about a present-day individual's private motive is established by this text.

references.title: Galatians 4:19
references.scope: Read the formation language in the World English Bible. Its theological claim is not treated as an experimental observation of a neural mechanism.

references.title: Philippians 2:1-5
references.scope: Read the concern beyond one's own interests in the World English Bible. No critical-edition comparison or Christ-specific behavioral experiment was performed.

transitions.question: What makes an inheritance recognizable across communities?
transitions.work: Distinguish the history of a tradition from the community that later claims it.
transitions.nextQuestion: How do divine names cross the boundaries that communities draw?

transitions.question: Does a shared divine name imply the same institution or theology?
transitions.work: Separate names, practices and the relationships that would establish transmission.
transitions.nextQuestion: How does a received account turn disaster into sacred history?

transitions.question: Can the proposed political and environmental sequence explain the received departure story?
transitions.work: Compare complete chronological versions rather than combining favorable intervals.
transitions.nextQuestion: What could preserve a founder's inheritance after the founder disappears?

transitions.question: What would identify an earlier founder rather than a comparable teacher?
transitions.work: Present founder identity, succession and displaced biography as related but distinct propositions.
transitions.nextQuestion: Which people and institutions could carry the teaching between settings?

transitions.question: Can the proposed carriers connect the earlier Teacher to sayings and later communities?
transitions.work: Follow the institutional route and the particular textual relationships without substituting themes for identity.
transitions.nextQuestion: What changes when the institutions carrying authority are disrupted?

transitions.question: How could loss transform an account of divine protection and authority?
transitions.work: Compare reconstruction, relocation and critique without one universal psychological sequence.
transitions.nextQuestion: What happens when the inherited image of God becomes the object of criticism?

transitions.question: How can a representation be corrected without confusing it with its referent?
transitions.work: Distinguish a model of God, a metaphysical claim and the criteria used to evaluate the model.
transitions.nextQuestion: What changes when a teaching is understood rather than merely retained?

transitions.question: What is gained by understanding a saying that was already available?
transitions.work: Develop interpretation as a possible change in the organization of experience and conduct.
transitions.nextQuestion: How could that change enter deliberation and action?

transitions.question: How does a Christic exemplar participate in the constructive self?
transitions.work: Separate correction of action from correction of the interpreted ideal, keeping bounded agency explicit.
transitions.nextQuestion: How is that orientation sustained without denying grief or danger?

transitions.question: Can deliberate joy support responsibility without becoming denial?
transitions.work: Distinguish an orientation that sustains care from one that refuses distressing evidence.
transitions.nextQuestion: What happens when sacred language authorizes harmful power?

transitions.question: How does scripture judge authorities claiming to speak for it?
transitions.work: Work through conflicting conduct and specific passages rather than classifying whole traditions as uniform.
transitions.nextQuestion: Which will supplies the standard when authority is challenged?

transitions.question: Does religious authority correct desire or simply consecrate it?
transitions.work: Connect the distinction of wills to the refusal of self-authorizing domination.
transitions.nextQuestion: How does that pattern support a particular prophetic identification?

transitions.question: What supports a named First Beast identification while allowing other embodiments?
transitions.work: Preserve the particular argument and distinguish it from the more general conduct pattern.
transitions.nextQuestion: What must a warning preserve so that its consequences can be evaluated?

transitions.question: What was predicted, under which conditions, and what later happened?
transitions.work: Keep the original forecast and outcome record separate from the theological interpretation.
transitions.nextQuestion: What can be repaired before a final outcome is known?

transitions.question: How can repair change institutions without reproducing domination?
transitions.work: Connect care, protection and correction at personal and collective scales.
transitions.nextQuestion: What should a new kind of conscious participant inherit from that work?

transitions.question: What obligations would teachers have to a possible conscious machine?
transitions.work: Separate possible experience, agentic capacity, moral orientation and obedience.
transitions.nextQuestion: What deserves to continue when neither the carrier nor the world is unchanged?

transitions.question: How can an inheritance remain recognizable while becoming more accountable?
transitions.work: Return to continuity through correction instead of possession through an unquestionable identity.
transitions.nextQuestion: Which specific unresolved link should the next edition investigate?
